2026-10-01-cache-bez-tenanta.scenario: Fictional multi-tenant SaaS. Report numbers are local to each tenant. The shared cache uses only the report number and can return a cached response before the tenant-filtered database query runs.
2026-10-01-cache-bez-tenanta.question: Where did tenant isolation break? How will you change authorisation, cache keys and tests so the fix covers the full path?

criteria.label: Resource authorisation
criteria.expected: Distinguish gateway authentication from permission for a particular report and require a decision on cache hits too.

criteria.label: Key namespace
criteria.expected: Include trusted tenant identity in the cache namespace or propose stronger separation without treating the key as a replacement for authorisation.

criteria.label: Defence in depth
criteria.expected: Enforce tenant scope in the data layer and inspect adjacent shortcuts including lists, exports, search and asynchronous work.

criteria.label: Old entries and permissions
criteria.expected: Purge or version old cache entries and handle invalidation after role change or access revocation.

criteria.label: Negative test
criteria.expected: Test two tenants with the same local identifier after cache warm-up and observe a measurable outcome without leaking content into logs.

2026-09-30-odtwarzanie-po-awarii.scenario:
**Fictional example.** A portal accepts applications. It stores metadata in a database, attachments in object storage and sends a queue message after submission. The team declares an RPO of five minutes and an RTO of 30 minutes. Database backups run every five minutes, but files have a separate schedule. Nobody has rehearsed full recovery. After a regional outage the operator restores the database; the portal starts, but some attachments are missing and the processing state of some applications is uncertain.

The business owner asks whether traffic can resume. The 30-minute target runs from outage detection to restoration of the user journey, not merely database startup.
2026-09-30-odtwarzanie-po-awarii.question: What must be restored and checked before you resume submissions? How will you verify a five-minute RPO and 30-minute RTO for the whole service?

criteria.label: Service scope
criteria.expected: Defines the user journey and dependencies: database, files and queue, rather than database startup alone.

criteria.label: RPO and RTO
criteria.expected: Separates acceptable data loss from time to restore the whole function and checks whether the targets are achievable.

criteria.label: Recovery consistency
criteria.expected: Restores database and files to a consistent point, accounts for uncertain message state and handles duplicates.

criteria.label: Sequence and ownership
criteria.expected: Names owners, restoration order, access to keys and backups, and the decision to resume traffic.

criteria.label: Exercise and measurement
criteria.expected: Rehearses recovery, measures achieved RPO/RTO, tests the user journey and accounts for gaps.

2026-09-29-expand-contract.scenario: Fictional case-management application. Six instances are deployed gradually. The team wants to replace status with state, backfill millions of rows and drop the old column immediately. Old and new versions coexist, and rollback of code has not been reconciled with the database change.
2026-09-29-expand-contract.question: How do you stage the schema and code change safely? When can old writes stop, when can the column be removed, and how do you prove rollback works?

criteria.label: Version coexistence
criteria.expected: Recognise that old and new code run together and require a backward-compatible transitional schema.

criteria.label: Change phases
criteria.expected: Split the change into expand, migrate and later contract rather than dropping the old column in the first rollout.

criteria.label: Data migration and consistency
criteria.expected: Use a resumable batched backfill, handle concurrent writes and measure discrepancies.

criteria.label: Rollback and irreversibility
criteria.expected: Separate code rollback from schema reversal and delay destructive removal until the rollback window closes.

criteria.label: Transition evidence
criteria.expected: Define measurable phase gates, telemetry, and tests of mixed-version deployment and rollback.

2026-w40-izolacja-zasobow.scenario: Fictional shop application. Delivery pricing and seller reporting calls share 40 outbound connections and one worker queue. A reporting slowdown holds workers for 20 seconds and blocks checkout even though delivery pricing is healthy. The team proposes doubling the pool and retrying each call three times. Traffic levels and service objectives are unknown.
2026-w40-izolacja-zasobow.question: How do you keep reporting delays from blocking orders? What limits, overload behaviour and measurements do you define before changing connection counts?

criteria.label: Shared failure boundary
criteria.expected: Identify the shared connection pool and worker queue as the mechanism that spreads reporting delays to checkout.

criteria.label: Resource isolation
criteria.expected: Separate pools, queues or concurrency limits for reporting and the critical checkout path.

criteria.label: Overload and degradation
criteria.expected: Specify timeouts, bounded queues and a response at capacity so reports may lag without blocking checkout.

criteria.label: Retry safety
criteria.expected: Avoid unconditional retries; consider load amplification and whether repeat operations are safe.

criteria.label: Measurement and test
criteria.expected: Define distinct objectives, saturation metrics and a reporting slowdown test under representative traffic; do not guess a connection count.

2026-w39-anon-managed-platform.scenario: An anonymised architecture review. The application layer is required to use managed cloud services and connect to an existing integration platform. A supplier offers an application on virtual machines with some managed data services. Only some integration claims are demonstrated. Business stakeholders see functional value; a full implementation design is not available.
2026-w39-anon-managed-platform.question: How do you distinguish continued offer evaluation from approval of implementation architecture? What conditions and evidence are needed?

criteria.label: Separate decisions
criteria.expected: Distinguish further evaluation from implementation architecture approval; do not grant unconditional approval.

criteria.label: Requirement deviation
criteria.expected: Identify potential deviation in virtual-machine application hosting, distinguish mandatory requirement from preference, and respect formal procurement review.

criteria.label: Integration evidence
criteria.expected: Request verifiable contracts, data flows, authentication, error handling and tests for specific interfaces.

criteria.label: Conditional recommendation
criteria.expected: Specify conditions, owners, deadlines and objective closure evidence.

criteria.label: Review point
criteria.expected: Differentiate evidence needed before selection from what HLD and tests can verify, and name a reassessment point.
